questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Besides the academic opportunities at UvA, it was crucial to me that my family and old friends live in the Netherlands. Besides being able to study at one of the best universities in Europe, I saw my exchange as a opportunity to connect with old friends and to be close to my family. Also, I really like Amsterdam as it is a city with an amazing vibe.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was OK. However, I think there are many ways in which the uni could improve their assistance to students. It was such a stressfull period before going on exchange.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Nothing. (But I missed out on introdays, so I am not sure how other students were received).

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was not easy at all, but I luckely found a room in a student flat, where a dutch girl and I switched housing as she was going to Copenhagen for the same amount of time. I found it via Facebook.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I felt like a got the real Amsterdam-experience, as I was living mostly with dutch students.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I did not have a bad experience regarding housing in Amsterdam, as I luckily found a place to stay. However, I heard from other students that they could not find a place to stay and had to live in weird places. I do not think that it is OK to accept so many student to Amsterdam, if there is not housing enough for them.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was very easy to registrate for courses at UvA.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was really easy to registrate the courses, as the course overview, the course description and the website where you should registrate your courses were all connected. It was really easy! And there was a great overview of the courses ones registred.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: My impression was that one could always seek contact if necessary. I think I contacted UvA in the registration process, and they answered almost immediatly. Really helpful!

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: 9/10. There was only one course I could not register for.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Register for the classes you find interesting, and maybe see if you are able to register for the bachelor-courses. Some of the Master-courses are part of a Master study-programme, and it can be hard to follow those courses as you do not have the same prior knowledge as the other students.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I think that the level of the courses at UvA are very high, but that the exams on the other hand are not as hard as in Copenhagen.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was very different. I found that the professors at UvA were really energetic and enthusiastic. There was constantly interaction between the teachers and the students, which made the classes more active and fun. And it was also very learnful.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: 1) International Responsibility, 2) Forced and Unforced Migration, 3) International Law and Sustainable Development, 4) Refugee Law, 5) Challenges in EU law

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
International Law and Sustainable Development was really an interesing course, and the teachers were great. The same goes for Forced and Unforced Migration. I also found Internaitonal Responsibility very interesting, however, many students found it hard. 

I would not recommend "Challenges in EU law" as I found the workload to be TOO MUCH for a 6 etcs course.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There were many opportunities to do non-school activity on campus.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Really everything! Yoga, soccer, knitting, acting etc.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would just enjoy the amazing city. Visit museums etc. You don't have to sign up for a non-academic activity in order to get most out of your exchange in Amsterdam.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Museums, Amsterdam Noord, Dutch "kroegen" etc.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was very easy for me as I am born in the Netherlands and I speak the language fluently.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Talk to them in class and go to the same parties as them - e.g. flatparties.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: That people are open-minded

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
It is really important to know that UvA can be/is a though university, and that you will not be able to have an exchange in Amsterdam that is "chill" like you might have heard from friends at other universities. UvA requires hard work. 

That said, Amsterdam is amazing! If you are a fan of Copenhagen, then you will love Amsterdam too.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Like mentioned above: be prepared for the workload at UvA. It is nothing like studying at UCPH.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: My amazing friends.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Adapting to the block-system at UvA. At UPCH we are used to more flexibility during a semester, whereas at UvA you just have to be on your toes from day one. You cannot just plan to read something later, because there will be no time.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: If shared, I want it to be anonymous.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
